name: Quaint Gothic 1894
designer: Unidentified in the consulted historical specimen
description: Contrasting sans-serif capitals with narrow hairlines and long descending strokes, revived from Ryan’s 1894 specimen.
observed: Capitals A–P and R–Y; figures 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9 and dollar sign on page 148. The 24–48-point impressions anchor the master; smaller impressions supply B, J, K, M, P and X.
reconstructed: Q and Z; figures 0, 3, 7 and 8; punctuation and remaining symbols. Lowercase input aliases capitals, as this historical specimen shows a capitals-only face. Spacing, kerning and harmonisation between optical sizes are new. The 1894 suffix dates the source, not a claimed first release.

sources.title: John Ryan Foundry, Latest and Standard Faces in Type (September 1894), p. 148
sources.rights: 1894 US publication, beyond the 95-year maximum term. Library of Congress scan; Archive metadata states that the Library of Congress is unaware of copyright restrictions. Metadata evidence retained in reference/ryan-rights.json.

revival.notes: See source/METHOD.md and source/tracing.json for reproducible crop selection, cleanup, scaling and companion drawings. No modern font outlines were used.
